There are three signal posts on the 20 km long railway track between stations P and Q. The distance between post 1 and post 2 is half the distance between post 2 and post 3. The distance from station P to its nearest post, post 1, is equal to the distance from station Q to post 3.

One day, the control centre at station P receives a message that a technical fault has occurred at post 3, and it must be repaired immediately. The repair team must start work within 40 minutes to avoid a major disruption. A maintenance trolley left station P at a speed of 30 km/h and passed post 1 after 5 minutes. If the trolley had doubled its speed after passing post 1, what would have been the maximum time the engineers would have had to fix the fault when it arrived at station P with the faulty equipment? Assume that loading and unloading of the equipment takes 1 minute.

The policemen at three different places on the ground blow a whistle after every 42 sec, 60 sec, and 78 sec respectively. They all starts blowing the whistle simultaneously at 9:00:00 pm, when they blow whistle again together, a gang of thieves were spotted by them. They were at a distance of 150 meters from policemen 1, 180 meters from policemen 2 and 100 meters from policemen 3. When the policemen start the chase, the thieves splitted in three direction and starts running. The speed of the thief 1 is 10 m/sec and speed of policemen is 12.5 m/sec, the speed of the thief 2 is 8 m/sec and speed of policemen is 11 m/sec. The speed of the thief 3 is 9.5 m/sec and speed of policemen is 10 m/sec. 

If all three thieves run in the same direction at their average speed, and the time taken by the policemen to catch them is equal to the average of the individual times taken to catch each thief, at what time (approximate) will the thieves be caught, and what distance will they cover during this time interval?

A conducting rod of length L = 1.5 m is placed horizontally on two smooth, frictionless, parallel conducting rails. The rails are connected at one end via a resistor of resistance R = 5 Ω, forming a closed rectangular circuit. A uniform magnetic field of magnitude B = 0.4 T is directed vertically upward, perpendicular to the plane of the rails. An external constant horizontal force of 3 N is applied to the rod, causing it to accelerate from rest along the rails. Neglect any friction, air resistance, and assume the resistance of the rod and rails is negligible compared to R.

You are required to find:

(a) The initial acceleration of the rod immediately after the force is applied.

(b) The direction of the induced current in the circuit (clockwise or counter-clockwise).

(c) The terminal velocity of the rod (if it exists).

F=m⋅a

Where: 

F is the force applied

m is the mass of the rod

The induced EMF ⁠<inlineMath>\left( \varepsilon  \right)⁠</inlineMath> in the circuit is given by:

⁠<inlineMath>\varepsilon  = BLv⁠</inlineMath>

Where:

B is the magnetic field strength

L is the length of the rod

v is the velocity of the rod

At terminal velocity, the net force acting on the rod is zero, meaning the force due to the applied force equals the magnetic drag force

The induced current in the loop is:

⁠<inlineMath>I = \frac{\varepsilon }{R} = \frac{{BLv}}{R}⁠</inlineMath> 

⁠<inlineMath>\varepsilon ⁠</inlineMath> is the induced EMF

R is the resistance of the circuit

L is the length of the rod

v is the velocity of the rod 

The magnetic force can be described by: 

⁠<inlineMath>{F_{magnetic}} = \frac{{{B^2}{L^2}v}}{R}⁠</inlineMath>

B is the magnetic field strength 

L is the length of the rod

v is the velocity of the rod

R is the resistance of the circuit

Evan is a clerk at a bookstore café. There he records the plays (Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, Crucible, Sales and Tempest). He also takes orders (Popcorn, Coffee, Soda, Nachos, Ice-cream and Candy) of six solo customers sitting at the counter (counters numbered 1 through 6), the order slips get mixed up.

Here’s what Evan remembers

  • The persons sitting at counters 3 and 4 bought either The Crucible or Death of a Salesman.
  • Nachos were ordered by the customer who bought The Crucible
  • The person in counter number 5 is a regular. She will not sit next to anyone who bought Macbeth and The Tempest.
  • The person who bought Soda is sitting at counter 6.
  • The person who bought Candy is sitting between the one who got Popcorn and the one who got Nachos.
  • The person who bought Othello is not sitting in counter 2, but is sitting between the person who bought The Crucible and the one who bought Hamlet.
  • The customer who bought Macbeth is not sitting next to the customer who bought Death of a Salesman.
  • The customer who bought Death of a Salesman did not purchase Ice Cream, Nachos, Soda, or Coffee.
  • The person who bought Othello also got a Coffee.

Which play did the one who bought ice cream get?

An inventor has three specially designed containers with capacities of 10, 15, and 25 liters. These containers are unique because they have a mechanism that allows the inventor to perform the following operations:

  1. Fill: Completely fill a container to its full capacity.
  2. Empty: Completely empty a container.
  3. Transfer: Transfer water from one container to another until one of them is either full or empty.
  4. Split: Split the water in a container equally into two parts, but this operation only works when the container has an even amount of water.

The inventor starts with the 25-liter container completely full, and the other two containers empty.
What is the smallest positive amount of water (in liters) that the inventor cannot measure using these containers and operations?

The designations are-IT coordinator, Computer Programmer, Data Analyst, Application Analyst, Web Developer, System Analyst and IT Analyst. Each person has been allocated the designation as per increasing order of their experience. The one with IT coordinator designation being the least experienced while the one with IT Analyst designation being the most experienced person respectively from the given statement. Only one person has less experience than Reba. The one has less experience than Reba likes Pineapple. Only one person has more experience than Riya. The one with System Analyst designation likes Litchi. Only two people have more experience than the one who likes Mango. Rubina likes Watermelon and has more experience than the one who likes Mango. Rita has less experience than the one with Application Analyst designation, but has more experience than the one who likes Banana. Radhika neither has the least experience nor does he work as a Web Developer. Rima is not a Web Developer. The one who like Grape is not an Application Analyst.
Who among the following is an Application Analyst?

Elara, Finn, Nyx, Orion, and Luna each set off on a solo journey, heading to five different cities around the world—Paris, Tokyo, Cairo, Sydney, and Rome. To match their personalities, each carried a uniquely coloured suitcase: one red, one black, one blue, one green, and one grey.
  • The traveller with the green suitcase flew to Cairo.
  • Elara does not have the black suitcase. The one who had the black suitcase didn’t go to Rome.
  • The person who carried the red suitcase didn’t go to Rome.
  • Luna did not travel to Rome.
  • The person with the grey suitcase is either Orion or the one who travelled to Tokyo.
  • Either Orion or the traveller with the blue suitcase went to Sydney.
  • Of Finn and the person who travelled to Paris, one had the black suitcase, the other had the red suitcase.
  • Neither Elara nor Nyx carried the blue suitcase.
  • The one with the red suitcase (not Elara) didn’t go to Paris.
Who went to Sydney?

An international flight operates a route from Airport J to City K. The details of the flight are as follows:

Distance: 1,200 km

Time Rules:

The flight also experiences a total delay of 45 minutes due to air traffic control.

Only one box is placed between the boxes having 125 and 115 balls. Box D has 160 balls. Box C is placed above Box F but neither of the boxes is placed in the topmost rack. Determine the total number of balls placed in uppermost and lowermost rack.

Arjun’s rank is a multiple of 5 but not the highest among all. There are two participants between Leela and Deepak. Arjun is in the seat opposite Manav, and neither is beside Leela. The participants sitting adjacent to the vacant chair hold ranks that are exactly one more than the ranks of the participants sitting on their other side. Who is to the immediate left of Deepak?

Direction: Read the following passage and solve the question based on it.

A bus transport service operates exactly three routes: route A, route B, and route C. The company issues three sets of passes for March and three sets for April—one set for each route for each its routes of the two months. The passes are designed under the following rules:
 
  • Each of the six sets of passes is printed in exactly one of the following colors: blue, orange, pink, white.
  • For each route, the March pass color is different from the April pass color.
  • For each month, all routes must have passes in different colors.
  • Exactly one set of March passes is pink.
  • For route C, either the March or April passes (but not both) are blue.
  • The March passes for route B are orange.
  • No April passes are orange.

If the March passes for route C are pink, then which one of the following must be true?

options.text: The route A passes for March are blue.
The route A passes for March are white.
The route A passes for April are pink.
The route C passes for April are blue.

questions.questionText:
The suffrage movement was a pivotal chapter in the struggle for gender equality, and women played a central role in driving it forward. Leaders like Susan B. Anthony, Emmeline Pankhurst, and Sarojini Naidu used public speaking, petitions, and peaceful protests to demand voting rights for women. These efforts were not limited to one country; women across the world organised marches, wrote letters, and formed groups to push for political inclusion. Many supporters argued that giving women the right to vote was a matter of justice and would lead to more balanced and inclusive governance. 

On the other hand, some opponents believed that women's involvement in politics would disrupt traditional social roles or distract from family duties. Despite such resistance, the determination of suffragists helped bring about significant legal changes, ultimately expanding democratic rights and setting the stage for future gender reforms.


Which of the following best reflects a balanced evaluation of both the supporting and opposing perspectives on women's participation in the suffrage movement, as discussed in the passage?

options.text: Advocates viewed suffrage as a path to equity and reform, while critics feared it would challenge deeply rooted societal structures.
Suffragists believed in the superiority of female leadership, whereas opponents doubted women’s intellectual abilities.
Supporters wanted women to replace men in politics, but traditionalists demanded complete political exclusion.
Campaigners prioritised individual rights, while detractors emphasised the need for women to focus on education over activism.

questions.questionText:
On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong took mankind’s first step on the lunar surface, uttering the now-iconic words, “That’s one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.” The Apollo 11 mission, executed by NASA, was hailed as a triumph of scientific achievement, engineering precision, and collective will. It marked a historic breakthrough not only for space exploration but also for humanity’s belief in pushing the boundaries of possibility.

Yet beneath the surface of celebration, the moon landing was deeply entangled in the geopolitical fabric of the Cold War. The U.S. space race against the Soviet Union had less to do with science and more to do with proving ideological superiority. The mission was as much a political performance as it was a scientific one, with the lunar flag and broadcast symbolising American dominance on a global stage.

Which of the following best supports the idea that the moon landing was more a political act than a scientific achievement?

options.text: The mission involved groundbreaking lunar research and the return of moon rock samples.
The globally broadcast event emphasised American presence and identity on lunar soil.
The mission sparked international space collaboration in the decades that followed.
Armstrong’s declaration aimed to unite humanity through a shared achievement.

questions.questionText:
India is the largest democracy in the world, with a population exceeding 1.4 billion people. The country follows a parliamentary system of government, where citizens elect representatives to the Lok Sabha (Lower House) and Rajya Sabha (Upper House) to make laws and policies. Every five years, general elections are held to choose the Prime Minister and members of Parliament. However, the process has also been marked by challenges such as corruption, voter manipulation, and inadequate marginalisation of represented groups. Despite these issues, India continues to uphold the values of democracy, ensuring equal rights and freedoms for all its citizens.

Based on the passage, identify the error and its correct usage

options.text: The term "general elections" should be replaced with "local elections" because it refers to choosing members of Parliament.
The term "parliamentary system" should be replaced with "presidential system" because India follows a presidential system of government.
The phrase "ensuring equal rights and freedoms for all its citizens" should be replaced with "ensuring equal rights for all its citizens" because freedoms are not granted in a democracy.

The phrase “inadequate marginalisation of represented groups” should be replaced with “inadequate representation of marginalised groups” because marginalisation, and not representation, is a valid challenge.

questions.questionText:
The hospitality industry has seen a significant shift with the increasing adoption of robotic technologies. Robots are now used for tasks such as check-in services, room deliveries, cleaning, and even concierge assistance. This rise in robotic integration has been driven by the demand for contactless services, especially during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as the need for operational efficiency. 
As a result, hotels and restaurants are witnessing reduced labour costs, quicker service delivery, and improved hygiene standards. However, this automation also raises concerns about job displacement and the diminishing human touch in guest interactions. The industry's challenge lies in balancing technological efficiency with personalized service to maintain customer satisfaction.
Which of the following best explains the cause-and-effect relationship highlighted in the passage?

options.text: Hotels use robots to attract tourists from abroad.
Robots are replacing chefs because guests prefer automation.
The need for contactless and efficient service led to increased use of robots in hospitality.
Increased robot usage is causing better customer relationships than human staff.

questions.questionText:
Tariffs, traditionally viewed as a means of economic protectionism, have increasingly become a double-edged sword in modern global trade. While they aim to support domestic industries by making foreign goods more expensive, the broader economic effects often raise critical concerns. Tariffs can lead to costlier raw materials and finished products, indirectly burdening domestic producers and consumers alike. 
In highly interconnected global markets, such measures may distort supply chains, provoke retaliatory tariffs, and reduce overall trade efficiency. Policymakers must therefore weigh immediate political or economic gains against the long-term risks of reduced competitiveness and strained international ties. Tariffs may serve strategic purposes, but are rarely without economic trade-offs.
What higher-order conclusion can be drawn from the passage about the use of tariffs in a globally interconnected economy?

options.text: Tariffs, though politically expedient, can introduce hidden inefficiencies that outweigh their intended benefits in open-market economies.
The imposition of tariffs is primarily a symbolic gesture, lacking measurable impact in interconnected trade networks.
Long-term national prosperity is best secured through sustained tariff regimes that prioritise domestic production over global collaboration.
Tariff policies serve as neutral tools that affect all economies symmetrically, regardless of their size or integration level.

questions.questionText:
Lateral inversion is the optical phenomenon where the left and right sides of an object appear reversed when reflected in a plane mirror. This reversal is not due to a change in the object itself but results from the way light rays bounce off the mirror surface and reach our eyes. Interestingly, the top and bottom of the object remain unchanged; only the horizontal orientation flips. This explains why written text appears backward in a mirror and why ambulance vehicles display the word "AMBULANCE" in reverse on their fronts so that drivers ahead see it correctly in their rear-view mirrors.

Though seemingly simple, lateral inversion reveals deeper ideas about symmetry and perception. Our brains are wired to interpret reflected images as if we are looking directly at the object, which creates a perceptual illusion of left and right switching. The concept also has real-world applications in physics, design, emergency services, and even robotics, where understanding mirrored behaviour is essential. Therefore, lateral inversion is not merely a visual curiosity but a principle that blends physics with cognitive science.

Which of the following best summarises the passage’s central insight into lateral inversion, integrating both its physical and cognitive dimensions?

options.text: Lateral inversion is a result of the brain’s inability to differentiate between real and reflected objects, causing confusion in everyday scenarios.
The mirror’s role in reversing only the vertical axis of an object explains why ambulance signs are readable in mirrors.
Lateral inversion illustrates how a physical phenomenon of reflection intersects with human perception, leading to practical applications and deeper insights into symmetry.
Lateral inversion is mainly a perceptual illusion with limited scientific or practical relevance beyond visual curiosities.

questions.questionText:
Plato believed that the world we see isn’t the real deal. He imagined a hidden realm of perfect, unchanging ideas behind everything. Nietzsche, on the other hand, thought we should let go of those old ideas of universal truth. When he said, ‘God is dead’, he wasn’t talking about religion alone; he meant that the traditional ideas people relied on to define right and wrong weren’t enough anymore.

Later philosophers pushed this idea even further. Hume argued that all we really know comes from our senses and even that might not be trustworthy. 

Kant took it a step further, saying we never experience reality directly; we only see a version of it shaped by our minds. More recently, thinkers like Derrida and Foucault suggested that maybe reality isn’t something objective at all, maybe it’s built by language, culture, and the people in power.

Which of the following best explains a cause-and-effect relationship from the ideas presented in the passage?

options.text: Plato’s belief in a hidden realm of perfect forms led later philosophers to embrace the idea of universal, unchanging truths
Nietzsche’s rejection of traditional ideas about truth and morality influenced later thinkers like Derrida and Foucault to question whether reality itself is shaped by language and power.
Hume’s scepticism about sensory knowledge led Kant to argue that humans can experience reality directly and objectively.
Kant’s philosophy directly caused Nietzsche to declare that ‘God is dead’ and reject all forms of moral thinking.

questions.questionText:
The psychological mindset of Indian women is shaped by a blend of tradition, societal expectations, and evolving modern influences. Historically, women have been expected to prioritize family duties over personal ambitions, leading to deeply ingrained notions of self-sacrifice and responsibility. However, with greater education, economic independence, and social awareness, many women are redefining their identities, and balancing career aspirations with cultural roles. Despite this progress, challenges such as gender bias, societal pressure, and internalised conditioning continue to impact decision-making and self-perception. The evolving mindset of Indian women reflects a transition from conformity to empowerment, where they strive for self-expression while navigating societal norms.

Which of the following statements contradicts the ideas presented in the passage?

options.text: Indian women are increasingly balancing personal aspirations with traditional responsibilities.
Education and economic independence have contributed to changing self-perceptions among Indian women.
The psychological outlook of Indian women remains entirely unchanged by modern influences.
Gender bias and societal expectations continue to influence the decision-making of Indian women.

questions.questionText:
The concept of formal examinations is believed to have originated in ancient China during the Han dynasty, where imperial exams were used to select candidates for government positions. These exams emphasised Confucian texts and aimed to reward merit over birthright. Over time, this model influenced other nations, including Britain, which adopted standardised testing during its colonial administration.

Eventually, examinations became a global system for evaluating knowledge and aptitude in education. However, critics argue that exams often prioritise memorisation over creativity and can place undue stress on students. Still, exams remain deeply rooted in educational systems as tools for measurement and selection.

What can be inferred about the long-term impact of exams based on the passage?

options.text: Despite cultural and educational shifts, exams have remained a dominant tool for measuring merit, though not without controversy.
The adoption of exams globally ensured the rise of democratic access to education for all social classes.
Exams became popular because they always supported innovative and flexible learning methods.
The exam system remained unchanged from ancient China to modern classrooms, proving its universal perfection.

questions.questionText:
The discovery of penicillin by Alexander Fleming in 1928 revolutionised medicine, leading to the development of antibiotics that could effectively treat bacterial infections. Before this breakthrough, minor infections often proved fatal, and there were limited treatment options for diseases such as pneumonia and strep throat. The mass production of penicillin during World War II saved countless lives and marked the beginning of the antibiotic era. However, the overuse of antibiotics in modern times has led to the rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, posing a significant challenge to global health. Scientists continue to research new antimicrobial solutions to combat this growing threat.

What best describes the tone of the passage?

The Earth’s ever-changing surface is largely the result of tectonic plate movement, a slow but powerful force that has shaped continents, formed mountains, triggered earthquakes, and created ocean basins over millions of years. The planet’s lithosphere is divided into rigid plates that float atop the semi-fluid asthenosphere. Driven by forces such as mantle convection and gravitational pull, these plates continuously shift, collide, diverge, and slide past each other.
At convergent boundaries, Earth's plates push against each other. This can form huge mountains like the Himalayas or deep valleys in the ocean. At divergent boundaries, the plates move away from each other. This lets hot, melted rock come up and make new land, like along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. At transform boundaries, the plates slide past each other sideways. This can cause strong earthquakes, like the ones near California’s San Andreas Fault.
Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: Tectonic plates are solely responsible for creating natural disasters like earthquakes and volcanoes.
The Earth's surface remains stable unless acted upon by volcanic eruptions at divergent plate boundaries.
The ongoing movement of tectonic plates is a fundamental force that continuously transforms Earth’s surface and holds vital clues to both its past and future.
Tectonic activity has mostly ceased in modern times, leaving behind static landforms and stable crustal boundaries.

questions.questionText:
Cloud storage has already revolutionised the way individuals and organisations manage data, but its future promises even more transformative shifts. One key development lies in edge-integrated cloud storage, where data processing occurs closer to the source such as IoT devices minimising latency and bandwidth use. This approach is critical for real-time applications like autonomous vehicles and smart city infrastructure.

Simultaneously, AI-powered storage management is expected to evolve rapidly. Intelligent systems could automatically organise, optimise, and secure cloud data, predicting storage needs or identifying vulnerabilities before they become critical. Moreover, decentralised cloud storage, leveraging blockchain, may offer enhanced privacy and user control by distributing data across networks rather than relying on centralised data centres. 

Which of the following inferences can most reasonably be drawn from the passage regarding the direction of cloud storage evolution?

options.text: The future of cloud storage will prioritise minimising hardware dependence by eliminating edge devices and decentralising all processes.
Advancements in cloud storage are primarily aimed at increasing storage space rather than enhancing security, speed, or accessibility.
The integration of edge computing, AI, and decentralised systems reflects a broader trend toward making cloud storage more intelligent, efficient, and secure.
As cloud storage becomes more complex, it will require users to manually manage and secure their data without algorithmic assistance.

questions.questionText:
A practical application of induced current is observed in electric turbines, where mechanical power is converted into electric power using rotating coils in a magnetic field. Similarly, transformers depend on electromagnetic induction to transfer electric power among circuits, adjusting voltage ranges for green power distribution. Induction cooking and wireless charging are different examples of how induced currents are harnessed for modern-day convenience.

However, induced currents additionally have drawbacks. In electrical machines and circuits, eddy currents (undesirable circulating currents triggered in conductive substances) can cause energy loss in the form of heat. Engineers design laminated cores in transformers and motors to limit these losses. Despite its challenges, electromagnetic induction remains an essential principle in the era of transmission of electrical energy, shaping present-day electronics.

Which of the following statements best presents a cause-and-effect relationship that challenges the view that induced currents are always advantageous?

options.text: Electromagnetic induction enables efficient energy transfer in transformers
Induced currents are used in various modern technologies, including induction stoves and wireless chargers, offering everyday convenience.
The generation of eddy currents due to electromagnetic induction causes energy loss in machines, prompting engineers to design laminated cores to reduce heat waste.
Faraday’s Law explains that the magnitude of induced current depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux, providing a basis for understanding induction in devices.

questions.questionText:
In 2023, a series of challenging environmental and economic factors combined to create a crisis for many households. A prolonged drought had severely impacted agricultural production, leading to a sharp rise in food prices. This situation caused significant financial strain on low-income households, resulting in increased demand for government assistance programmes. In response, the government expanded food subsidies and introduced relief measures to support affected families.

Select the primary cause and effect in the given scenario:

options.text:
Cause: Prolonged drought led to reduced agricultural production.
Effect: The government halted food subsidies and relief measures.

Cause: Rise in food prices due to agricultural decline.
Effect: Increased demand for government assistance programmes.

Cause: Lack of government support for farmers and agricultural workers.
Effect: Consumers shifted to alternative food sources.

Cause: Increased demand for government assistance programmes.
Effect: Farmers adopted new irrigation techniques.

questions.questionText:
Federalism in India is a system of governance in which power is constitutionally divided between the central government and the state governments. The Indian Constitution establishes a unique form of federalism that balances unity and regional autonomy.

Unlike traditional federal systems, India has unitary features such as a strong central government, emergency provisions (Article 356), and the ability of Parliament to legislate on state matters in certain situations. However, cooperative federalism is emphasised through mechanisms like the Finance Commission and the Inter-State Council, ensuring coordination between different levels of government.

While federalism in India ensures regional autonomy and administrative efficiency, it also faces challenges such as conflicts between states, centralisation of power, and financial dependence of states on the central government.

 

Which of the following is an argument against federalism in India?

options.text: It allows regional autonomy, respecting cultural and linguistic diversity.
It decentralises power, making governance more efficient.
It leads to conflicts between the central and state governments, slowing policymaking.
It ensures better cooperation between different levels of government.

questions.questionText:
In a formal company, communication plays a critical role in making sure that goals are met efficiently and constantly. The sorts of communication normally fall into three classes: downward, upward, and horizontal. Downward communication involves messages from higher to lower level within the hierarchy, such as instructions, feedback, and policies ensuring that the strategic vision is implemented operationally. Upward communication, lets in subordinates to share reports, demanding situations, and recommendations with their superiors, fostering transparency and responsiveness. 
Horizontal communication occurs among peers or departments at the same level, important for coordination and collaboration across capabilities. Increasingly, formal organizations are incorporating digital platforms to facilitate all three sorts, allowing asynchronous but traceable exchanges. However, demanding situations remain in preserving clarity, handling quantity, and heading off misinterpretation mainly in highly based environments. 
Which of the following best reflects the author’s underlying concern about communication in formal organizations?

options.text: Digital communication tools are replacing traditional forms of communication entirely in organizations.
While structured communication types support organizational functioning, modern tools introduce new challenges in ensuring effectiveness.
Upward communication is inherently less valued in formal settings, leading to decision-making delays.
Horizontal communication leads to informal alliances that weaken the formal structure of organizations.

questions.questionText:
Psychological well-being plays a critical role in maintaining overall health and productivity. It was found in studies that individuals with good mental health are more likely to build strong relationships and cope effectively with stress. On the other hand, untreated psychological issues such as anxiety and depression can lead to severe consequences, including physical illnesses and diminished quality of life. Advocates argue that investing in mental health resources not only benefits individuals but also reduces societal costs associated with lost productivity and healthcare expenses. Critics, however, contend that limited budgets should prioritise physical health interventions, as their impact is more immediate and measurable.

Which of the following arguments supports the importance of investing in psychological well-being?

options.text: Studies suggest that individuals with good mental health are more productive and resilient.
Physical health interventions have a more immediate and measurable impact.
Mental health issues overshadow underlying physical illnesses and diminished quality of life.
Limited budgets should prioritise physical health interventions over psychological health.

questions.questionText:
Statement:

Nazism rose to power in Germany by exploiting economic hardship, nationalism, and propaganda, leading to World War II and the Holocaust. The rise of Nazi Germany exposed the dangers of totalitarianism, prompting global efforts to prevent the resurgence of such ideologies.

Inferences: 

Unchecked nationalism and propaganda can manipulate societies toward destructive outcomes, demonstrating how authoritarian regimes can rise by exploiting public sentiment and economic instability.

Which of the following high-order inferences can be drawn from the statement and the inferences provided from the rise and fall of Nazism?

options.text: Societies facing economic hardship are always destined to embrace authoritarianism.
The fall of a totalitarian regime ensures that its ideology will never return.
Controlling public perception through propaganda can enable the rise of destructive ideologies.
Military strength alone determines the longevity of a political movement.

questions.questionText:
Paris, often referred to as the "City of Light," is home to some of the world’s most iconic monuments that reflect not just architectural brilliance but also the evolving identity of France. The Eiffel Tower, once criticized as a monstrous addition, is now celebrated as a global symbol of modernity and innovation. The Notre-Dame Cathedral, with its centuries-old Gothic design, embodies the spiritual and historical heart of Paris, having witnessed revolutions, coronations, and cultural rebirths. 
Meanwhile, the Arc de Triomphe stands as a tribute to military valour and national pride, linking past victories to the collective memory of the French people. Interestingly, newer monuments like La Défense’s Grande Arche embrace futuristic aesthetics and economic ambition, signifying how Paris blends tradition with transformation. Collectively, these monuments serve not only as tourist attractions but as evolving narratives of a nation's aspirations, resilience, and reinvention.
Which of the following interpretations most accurately captures the author's nuanced view of the monuments of Paris?

options.text: The monuments of Paris are intentionally preserved relics that resist contemporary reinterpretation, emphasizing stability over change.
Parisian monuments act as dynamic cultural texts, reflecting both the continuity of tradition and the evolution of national consciousness.
The significance of Parisian monuments lies mainly in their architectural grandeur, which overshadows any symbolic relevance.
Monuments in Paris reveal a nostalgic resistance to modernization, representing a longing for pre-revolutionary France.

questions.questionText:
Scientific inventions have long been regarded as milestones of human progress, shaping societies and transforming the way people interact with the world. From the printing press revolutionizing knowledge dissemination to electricity redefining industries, inventions have largely been seen as forces of advancement. However, the impact of scientific discoveries is rarely one-dimensional. The development of nuclear energy, for instance, presented an unparalleled energy source while simultaneously introducing the threat of mass destruction. Similarly, artificial intelligence (AI) has enhanced automation and efficiency but raised concerns regarding job displacement, ethical dilemmas, and loss of human control over decision-making processes. 

Even medical breakthroughs, such as genetic engineering, have sparked debates on ethical boundaries, unintended genetic consequences, and potential misuse. Thus, while scientific inventions have propelled humanity forward, they also demand careful regulation, ethical consideration, and a balanced approach to mitigate potential risks.

Which of the following best opposes the central argument of the passage?

options.text: Scientific inventions, though transformative, must be strictly regulated to prevent unforeseen consequences, as history has repeatedly demonstrated how technological advancements can lead to ethical crises and societal harm.

While scientific inventions present ethical challenges, their overall contributions to human progress far outweigh potential risks, as seen in advancements in medicine, communication, and space exploration.

The impact of scientific discoveries should not be judged in terms of ethical concerns alone; rather, the focus should be on how effectively these inventions can be used to improve economic productivity and industrial growth.

Although some scientific inventions carry risks, history shows that human ingenuity and policy interventions have consistently addressed and mitigated such dangers, making ethical concerns secondary to innovation.
